principe.texte: On Jamii, orange always means the same thing: it is proven. A project that responds, a task delivered on time, an answer accepted by the person who asked.

accueil.decrireBesoin: I have a need for my business

sectionMissions.titre: Missions: hire a developer, milestone by milestone
sectionMissions.intro: A small business, a shop or an association has a specific need. It posts it as a mission, developers from across the continent offer their services, and the work is split into milestones, each with its own amount and timeframe.

1.texte: Describe the need, the budget and the skills. The mission is public, or visible only to the developers you invite.

2.texte: Developers offer their services. You talk with them, pick one, then they send you a quote split into milestones.

3.texte: The developer delivers each milestone. You accept it or ask for a revision. Everyone always sees the next step.

4.texte: The client declares the payment, the developer confirms receiving it. At the end, each leaves a review for the other.

points: Start from your need, or from the plan prepared with Ayo.
Compare proposals and profiles before choosing.
Pay milestone by milestone, never all at once.
Find missions that need your skills.
Send a clear quote: milestones, amounts, timeframes.
Ask for an extension if needed, and a moderator settles any disagreement.

argent.texte: Jamii does not collect the payment: the client pays the developer directly, then each declares it in the mission (“paid”, then “received”). Everyone sees where each milestone stands.

sectionHackathons.titre: Run a challenge, from the first sign-up to the winners
sectionHackathons.intro: A school, a company, a community or a city launches a challenge. Jamii handles sign-ups, teams, hand-ins and jury scoring, online, on site or both.

1.texte: The organizer sets the calendar, the team size, the scored criteria and their weight, the prizes and the code of conduct.

2.texte: Open sign-up or by application. People on their own find each other on the “Looking for a team” board.

3.texte: Each team hands in its product link and answers the questions. The hand-in can be edited until the deadline.

4.texte: The jury scores each criterion from 1 to 5, never its own team's project. The organizer confirms the winners.

hackathon.texte: A short, intense event, online, on site or hybrid. Teams build a product that works.

challenge.texte: A challenge over several weeks, to go further: teams hand in a finished project before the deadline.

concours.texte: A company or a school sets a real problem and rewards the best ideas, with prizes in money or in services.

prix.texte: Each prize can have an amount, or none at all: visibility or hosting, for example.

faq.intro: Answers to the questions we hear most, feature by feature.

quoi.r: The exchange platform for African developers. Find teammates, talk in communities, answer small businesses' needs, and keep your projects alive all the way to going online.

connexion.r: With GitHub if you're a developer, with Google, or with your e-mail address: we send you a sign-in link, no password to remember.

pasDev.q: I'm not a developer. Is Jamii for me?
pasDev.r: Yes. A shop, an association or a small business describes its need in its own words. Jamii's assistant turns it into a clear plan, says what already exists, and who can build the rest.

cercle.r: A group of 4 to 6 developers who take turns building each member's project. At each turn, the whole circle helps one member move forward.

paiement.r: The work is split into milestones, each with its amount. The client pays the developer directly, then each declares it in the mission: “paid”, then “received”. Jamii does not collect the money.

hackathon.r: Anyone signed in: a school, a company, a community. The hackathon stays a draft, visible only to you, until you publish it. It has its own discussion space, criteria and jury.

vitrine.q: How does a project get into the showcase?
vitrine.r: When a project is online, Jamii checks that it responds, then shows it in the showcase with its team. A link that no longer responds does not appear.

langues.r: French and English. The assistant answers in the language of the person writing to it.

donnees.r: We collect the minimum. From your profile, you can export all your data or delete your account, at any time.

sectionCercles.titre: Circles: an African tradition, adapted to software
sectionCercles.intro: Take turns building each member's project. 4 to 6 developers commit together: at each turn, the whole circle builds one member's project.

histoire.accroche: A tontine is not only about money.

tradition.texte: The tontine is known all over the continent. A group pools money and, at each turn, one of its members receives the whole amount.

esprit.texte: What holds a tontine together is the gathering. Neighbours, colleagues and friends meet, talk, share their news and support each other.

jamii.texte: Jamii wants to bring African developers together, so it was natural to start from this spirit of sharing. In a circle, we don't pool money, we pool work.

histoire.citation: Money sets the rhythm. The community is the real goal.

part.tontine: Each member gives money, on a fixed date.
part.cercle: Each member gives time and skills.

tour.tontine: At each turn, one member receives what the group gathered.
tour.cercle: At each turn, the whole circle builds one member's project.

ensemble.tontine: People meet, talk and help each other.
ensemble.cercle: We learn from each other, turn after turn.

paralleles.titre: From the tontine to the circle

1.texte: Create a circle or join one. It brings together 4 to 6 developers who commit together.

2.texte: Each member submits the idea of the project they want built during their turn.

3.texte: The order of turns is drawn at random by Jamii: nobody chooses who goes first.

4.texte: The whole circle builds the turn's project, then delivers it. The Griot, the assistant that plans and sums up the turn, helps things move.
